q. Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue. West Triangle. Quezon City http: /lwww. dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. 0 3 NOV 2017 00 S. 2DL AITY. MARIE ANGELICA THELMO Chief Legislative Officer Office of Senator Grace Poe Room 525, Senate of the Philippines GSIS Financial Center, CCP Complex Pasay City Dear Atty. Thelmo: This has reference to your letter dated 4 May 2017 requesting for this Department's legal opinion on whether the provincial government has the power to set tariffs for the provision of used water services within its jurisdiction and whether Local Government Units (LGUs) have the power to approve used water tariff. First and foremost, please be apprised of the definition of tariff. As defined, tariff is (a) a schedule of duties imposed by a government on imported or in some countries exported goods and a duty or rate of duty imposed in such a schedule; and (b) a schedule of rates or charges of a business or a public utilityl. Considering the use of the word "tariff' and the reference made to "used water services" in the subject query, may we provide the discussion presented hereunder in an attempt to properly address the subject matter. Section 133(d) of R.A. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC), provides as follows: "Section 133. Common Limitations on the Taxing Powers of Local Government Units. - Unless otherwise provided herein, the exercise of the taxing powers of provinces, cities, municipalities, and barangays shall not extend to the levy of the following: (d) Customs duties, registration fees of vessel and wharfage on wharves, tonnage dues, and all other kinds of customs fees, charges and dues except 1 Merriam-Webster since 1828

wharfage on wharves constructed and maintained by the local government unit concerned; (Emphasis Supplied) In the Philippines, import duties are imposed, generally in ad valorem form, on articles entering the country in accordance with their corresponding schedules and classifications as provided under Section 104 of the Tariff and Customs Code of the Philippines (TCCP) of 1978, as amended. With the exception of certain articles which can be imported duty-free, upon compliance with certain prescribed conditions or formalities. Hence, if the situation contemplated is that involving LGUs adjacent to territories outside the customs territory of the Philippines such as ECOZONEs and FREEPORTs, the considered view thereon is that the concerned LGUs are bereft of authority to impose tariff on the importation or exportation of used water. On the other hand, if what is contemplated is for the LGUs to impose schedule of water rates, this level is of the view that LGUs are stripped of authority to impose water rates as the same is tantamount to interfering with the internal as well as, external dealings of the water company. Nonetheless, if what is being referred to is the imposition of "fees" or "charges" by LGUs on the services provided by water companies, the same may find basis on Section 129 of the LGC, to wit: "Section 129. Power to Create Sources of Revenue. - Each local government unit shall exercise its power to create its own sources of revenue and to levy taxes, fees, and charges subject to the provisions herein, consistent with the basic policy of local autonomy. Such taxes, fees, and charges shall accrue exclusively to the local government units. " Thus, we recommend that the word "tariff' be changed to the words used by the LGC to be consistent therewith. Further, the letter request mentioned that the setting and monitoring of tariff rates for used water services appear to be within the authority of the provincial government. This position is said to have been anchored on Section 17, paragraph 3 of the LGC, which gives authority to provincial governments to effect infrastructure projects such as drainage and sewerage facilities to service the needs of the province. The Department is of a different view, Section 17, paragraph 3 of the LGC merely contains enumeration of the basic services and facilities to be provided by provincial governments. The setting of taxes, fees and charges by an LGU is within the domain of its taxing and revenue-raising powers governed by the provisions under Book II of the LGC on Local Taxation and Fiscal Matters.

Thus, insofar as the imposition of local taxes, fees and charges on specific services concerning used water is not constrained by the linmitations on LGUs' taxing power, such imposition or approval of rates thereof is authorized. Cc: We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Very truly yours, By Aut of the Secretary: AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary - OUSLG IO- 0-0 Kon. Irvin Paulo "PAUi" C. Tapales 4th floor, Antipolo City Hall Carigma St., Cor. M.L Quezon St. Antipolo City
